• The bug is in the `build_search_url` function. When a `language` is provided, the code appends `&q=language:{language}` to the URL. However, the URL already contains a `q` parameter from the initial `q` variable. The GitHub API only allows one `q` parameter — having two `q` parameters means the second one will override the first (or GitHub will only recognize one of them).

  So the search query `created:>2023-01-01` will be lost when a language filter is provided, because the language filter uses `&q=` which creates a duplicate `q` parameter instead of appending to the existing one.

• The bug is that the function uses `&q=language:{language}` when a language is specified, creating a second `q` parameter. The GitHub API only accepts a single `q` parameter, so the original query (`created:>2023-01-01`) is overwritten or ignored, breaking the intended date filter. The language term should instead be appended into the existing `q` value, e.g. `url += f"+language:{language}"`.
